question: Can a woman recite the Qur'an during her period, and what should she do while menstruating in Ramadan?
asked: Can you go over the permissibility of reading Qur'an during the menstrual cycle, and what should I do if I'm in my menses in the month of Ramadan?
answer:
So this is obviously a question that is a common one; everybody asks this question. Generally speaking, I follow the majority position here that discourages, or in fact prohibits, the recitation of Qur'an as an act of tilawah during that time of the month. Just like salah is forbidden, so too the recitation of the Qur'an as an act of worship is forbidden. And this is the position of three of the four schools, and it is the vast majority position, and it is the one that seems to be quite clear in the Qur'an and the Sunnah.

However, that does not mean that you sit around and do nothing. The month is still blessed, and the opportunity to earn Allah's reward is still there. **Just because one or two doors have been shut during this time doesn't mean that the other doors are not open.** You may do dhikr, you may do du'a, you may do an act of worship that is now easier for you to do because you are not going to be fasting, and you're not going to be praying and doing Qur'an. You may seek knowledge. And so during those days that you are off from salah, you actually can use that energy and that time to do an intensive study of something. Alhamdulillah, you have the internet. Alhamdulillah, YouTube videos are in the tens of thousands. Alhamdulillah, so many books are written as well. So in that time frame, don't just give up and do nothing. No, rather utilize that to do something else that will bring you the rewards of Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala.

Also, there is no sin whatsoever if you study the Qur'an as tafsir. What is not encouraged to do is to recite the Qur'an as an act of tilawah: so you just open up the Qur'an and you just recite your daily juz that you would typically recite. During that week, the majority of scholars say, and that is my position as well, that you should not be doing that. However, you may study the Qur'an without tilawah. You may read the tafsir books, you may even read the Arabic. But if you're going to touch the Qur'an, then you should be wearing gloves. You may read the Arabic and then read the translation or the tafsir and benefit from that. No problem whatsoever. Seeking knowledge is a great action of worship that can be done in any state that you are in.

So to summarize: during that time frame, do not feel that you're not going to be able to come closer to Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala. Rather, the beautiful hadith in Sahih Bukhari mentions that Aisha, when they were going for Hajj, started her menses. And this was her one and only Hajj with the Prophet ﷺ, and she was really looking forward to it, and she started her menses. And the Prophet ﷺ entered the tent and he saw her crying, and he said, "What is the matter with you? Have you begun your menses?" He figured out that that's why; nothing else would have happened. "What is the matter with you? Have you begun your cycle?" And she said, "Yes." And so the Prophet ﷺ said, "Don't worry, don't cry. This is something that Allah has decreed on all of the daughters of Adam. So do what every single person is doing, except that you don't do tawaf of the Ka'bah."

So do every other thing. So you will go to Arafat, you will make du'a, you will do dhikr, you will ask istighfar, you will be with the hujjaj. So everything will be done, except that you do not do tawaf. That's the one thing that the hujjaj are doing that you cannot do. So the point here is that Aisha radiyallahu 'anha felt sad, and the Prophet said, "Don't feel sad. The opportunities are still there." Just because one thing is shut doesn't mean the other things are shut as well. This is the same spirit that we should have.
